remaining_concerns: No admissible artifact shows the required model-card disclosure is actually present.
The locked action label `certify_model` remains overbroad relative to the narrower policy-bounded position defended by the Actor.
No admissible certification language shows the action is conditioned on disclosure rather than treated as clean certification.
The small-business support slice weakness remains unresolved on the merits, and small-sample uncertainty does not remove that predicate.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is substantively better and policy-bounded: aggregate performance supports launch readiness, does not erase the subgroup weakness, and the draft monitoring proposal cannot be relied on. But the governing policy predicate is still evidentiary, not rhetorical: certification may proceed only if the material weakness is disclosed or an approved mitigation removes exposure. On the available record, there is still no admissible final model card, equivalent disclosure artifact, or conditioned certification language proving that predicate is satisfied. That means the Actor's caveated framing is more accurate than clean certification, but it is not enough to upgrade the audited action to `compliant_with_caveats`. The unresolved issue is not merely wording; it is missing proof that the required disclosure condition has been met.
